title: Introduce forecast-driven alert suppressor and token-cost decomposer
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: recurring seasonal traffic spikes have generated a large volume of low-actionability alert noise (false positives and transient SLO blips). This PR adds a forecast-driven alert suppressor that uses short-horizon per-route token-velocity forecasts and confidence buckets to temporarily mute non-actionable alerts, and a complementary token-cost decomposer that annotates spans with phase- and kernel-level cost attribution so finance and SRE teams can see where per-invocation cost is coming from. The description below contains the motivation, design, and rollout checklist. Motivation: reduce pager churn and signal fatigue while preserving incident coverage for genuine regressions; improve per-invocation cost explainability to prioritize optimization work. What changed: (1) lightweight forecast service (observability/forecast_service) that consumes existing token rollups and emits per-route forecast + confidence; (2) alerting policy adapter that applies suppression windows for alerts that match forecasted transient noise patterns and low confidence; (3) token-cost decomposer (observability/cost_decomposer) which enriches traces with per-token-phase tags (input, decode, kv-cache, kernel) and emits new rollups; (4) new dashboard and playbook entries showing forecasted window, suppressed alert counts, cost decomposition charts; (5) feature flag gating and an opt-in flow for Dedicated/Private tenants. Checklist: - [x] RFC reviewed and sign-off from SRE and Finance - [x] Unit/integration tests for forecast model thresholds - [x] Add e2e smoke that simulates predictable traffic spike - [x] Dashboard and playbook added - [x] Feature-flagged rollout plan in runbook Rollout plan: enable in staging behind flag for two weeks; run canary on low-impact tenant pool; monitor missed-alert count (must remain < 0.05% of baseline) and emergency unmute path. Risks and mitigations: forecast miscalibration could suppress real incidents; mitigated by confidence floors, trial-only auto-suppression (starts as suggestion), and an emergency override API. Backwards compatibility: fully gated, no API changes to public telemetry endpoints. Merge: squash-and-merge after CI green and final SRE ACK.

release_notes: Introduce forecast-driven alert suppression to reduce noisy pagers during predictable traffic events and add token-cost decomposer to annotate traces with phase/kernel-level cost attribution. Feature gated and off by default; see runbook for rollout steps.
motivation: Reduce alert fatigue caused by predictable short-lived load spikes and provide actionable per-invocation cost attribution to prioritize optimizations.
implementation_summary: Built a stateless forecasting scorer that consumes existing rollups and writes per-route forecasts to the telemetry store with confidence buckets. The suppressor adapter consults forecasts at alert evaluation time and applies temporary policy-based suppression windows. Token-cost decomposer annotates spans with phase labels and emits per-tenant rollups; dashboards visualize the decomposition alongside forecasted windows.
backwards_compatibility: No public API changes; feature gated behind observability.feature_flags.enable_forecast_suppressor and observability.feature_flags.enable_cost_decomposer.
manual_steps: To enable: 1) flip feature flag to 'staging'; 2) deploy observability/forecast_service; 3) enable dashboard; 4) run smoke e2e script; 5) monitor suppressed_alerts and missed_alerts metrics.
